title: A fair price for a coin game?
hook: Flip until tails; the payout doubles with each flip. What should entry cost?

knows: an average payout is total winnings divided by plays
doesNotKnow: that an average can be made mostly of rare big payouts
that a typical player may never see it

misconception: A game with typical payouts of a few dollars cannot have a high fair price.
objective: The learner can say that the fair price is the long-run average payout ($20 here), that it comes from rare big wins, and that most plays pay $4 or less.
keyState: A price chosen and at least 200 games played; on the click path 550 games with average $25.79, median $4 and biggest $8,192 (58% of all winnings).

claims.text: The game: flip a fair coin until the first tails, at most 20 flips; first tails on flip k pays $2^k, and 20 heads pays $0.
claims.source: Rules shown on the stage and in the question; payout() in model.ts.

claims.text: The exact fair price is $20: each k from 1 to 20 adds 2^k x (1/2)^k = $1 to the average payout.
claims.source: Sum over k = 1..20 of 2^k (1/2)^k = 20 (fairPrice() in model.ts, recomputed in node). The probability of first tails on flip k is (1/2)^k. | v2 (2026-10-14): options parallel and payouts spelled out; reveal shows the $1-per-flip working; previous verification void, needs re-check.
P(first tails on flip 1) + P(flip 2) = 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4; payouts $2 and $4.

claims.text: In the stage's seeded run, the average payout after 550 games is $25.79, the median payout is $4 and the biggest payout is $8,192, which is 58% of all money paid out.
claims.source: Game g uses mulberry32(2500 + g), untuned (first seed tried). One early $8,192 payout lifts this run above the typical case: over 400 other seed sets of 550 games the average had median $11.6, 10th to 90th percentile $8.1 to $25.7 (min $6.2, max $969), and only 13.5% reached $20 or more.

claims.text: The running average can sit well below $20 for many games because the big payouts are rare, so a run is not a reliable guide to the fair price.
claims.source: Spread across seeds in claim 4: the median 550-game average is $11.6, below $20; the variance of one payout is the sum of 4^k (1/2)^k = about 2.1 million.

claims.text: The profit readout is total payouts minus price times games played.
claims.source: profit = summary(n).total - price x n in Demo.tsx.

recall.question: A game pays $1 million with chance 1 in 1,000 and nothing otherwise. Is $1,000 a fair entry price?
options: No, it must cost less than $1
recall.why: Fair price equals the average payout: 1/1000 x $1,000,000 = $1,000. Most plays pay nothing, but the rare big wins carry the average.
